title: Comprehensive Functional UI Automation
scope: All currently mounted product functionality in packaged Windows desktop and local Chrome thin client, with managed identity/PostgreSQL/TLS and installed-runtime cases as explicitly named controlled layers. Also retain reusable tests for intentionally unmounted API/component surfaces without exposing them as product navigation.
sourceAuthority: Implemented host wiring and behavioral tests
inventoryMethod: Read actual desktop/thin route registries and App page wiring.
Inspect each mounted page, feature components/hooks, shared presenters and public contracts.
Trace declared behavior through canonical architecture and current ADR/readiness boundaries.
Crosswalk existing component, integration, Playwright and physical AI harnesses before proposing missing coverage.
At implementation start regenerate route/tab/action capability census and explain every unmapped supported action; this preparation is not an exhaustive Cartesian behavior proof.

surfaceCensus.countMeaning: File count is inventory context, not executed coverage or completeness.
intentionalHostDifferences: Desktop has Train Model and native runtime/settings controls; thin Models currently exposes browse/inventory only.
Thin client exposes Security status and command/read projections of server-owned lifecycle; it does not gain Electron filesystem/window/runtime authority.
Published desktop runtime renderer currently exposes controlled conversation, not a generic secured-record/review application UI.

Server has no separate operator graphical application; UI tests cover server-backed functionality through its mounted thin client, while CLI/operator and API-only surfaces retain their own non-UI tests.

executionStrategyOptions.label: Extend the existing layered UI toolchain
executionStrategyOptions.summary: A finite source-linked scenario manifest maps every mounted supported capability to behavioral UI tests and a real desktop/thin-client journey. Parameterized variants run at the narrowest meaningful layer; named managed/native/physical-runtime witnesses remain separate. Reuse existing Playwright/Vitest and owned host harnesses.
tradeoffs: Keeps real UI coverage while avoiding repeated large model loads and duplicate workflows
Requires explicit classification so deterministic workers are never mislabeled real inference
Fits the current laptop by running one browser/desktop worker and serial resource-heavy checks
consequences: Add missing scenarios, execute them and repair reproduced defects in cohesive vertical slices
Publish a machine-readable coverage/evidence ledger with genuine gaps visible
No new automation framework dependency or product architecture is needed

executionStrategyOptions.label: Require complete host/runtime execution for every UI variant
executionStrategyOptions.summary: Use the same scenario inventory but make full packaged desktop and managed-browser real-runtime journeys the primary gate for each supported task, input, settings and failure variation.
tradeoffs: More direct integration coverage for every combination
Much longer and more fragile runs, repeated model loading and higher RAM/VRAM demands
Unavailable native/provider/runtime environments block a larger part of the roadmap
consequences: Requires a provisioned qualification environment for many variants and more external execution authority
Fewer isolated failures; diagnostics and rerun costs increase
Existing component and adapter checks still remain necessary for owned invariants

adjacentCohesionAuditProposal: The scenario manifest and harness are delivered with first Data/Context/AI consumers, not as a separate test-only foundation increment.

The authoring-to-release slice delivers independently useful Assets/System coverage over immutable definition/release boundaries; separating it from Data/Context avoids one unreasonably large review across independent subsystems.

The last slice is justified by actual managed/native/physical environment admission and cross-surface recovery qualification, not merely final report writing. Keep its operational UI consumers and their recovery regressions together.
closureContractProposal: Regenerate the finite route/tab/action/task/host census at implementation start and map every supported capability to stable scenario IDs, exact assertions, test file and evidence tier. No unaccounted reachable action is complete.

Every scenario has an actual user-visible outcome oracle; business data, immutable bytes/digests, reopened values or verified denial are observed through authoritative boundaries, not only click success or snapshots.

Execute all applicable new/reused scenarios on current source, diagnose each reproduced failure, repair in-scope defects at the owning layer and rerun relevant regressions. Unexpected missing capability becomes a recorded finding, never an invented pass.

No unresolved in-scope defect is hidden by retries/skips/quarantine. Deferred product decisions or unavailable technical environments remain explicit blockers until actually resolved or user revises scope.
All criteria are executable by agents. Human acceptance remains offline and never makes the technical roadmap incomplete.
Do not change existing completion statuses or accepted historical evidence as part of this planning pass. Exact new evidence can support an existing owner only through its own governed process.

Each reproduced defect first has an owning expected contract and red regression when practical, then an owning-layer fix and successful rerun. A missing product capability or new authority/design remains an explicit decision gate.

Each approved increment includes security-impact-reviewed, candidate-bound focused check receipts and separate-invocation review. As AI functionality is in scope, initialize completionSuite all; reserve aggregate run until all implementation chunks are complete.

Use focused component/client/host tests while implementing. At final boundary run npm run test:all, docs:check, architecture:check and affected builds/package plus agent-support/dependency gates only when their trigger changes. Named physical/managed/packaged tests remain explicit and cannot be inferred from test:all.
ciAndFailurePolicyProposal: Reuse Node/Vitest focused UI gates and the one-worker Playwright harness. Add a finite capability/scenario coverage check rather than a new automation stack.
Run deterministic synthetic UI branching in normal focused feedback; packaged Windows, managed OIDC/PostgreSQL/TLS, physical runtime and named performance profiles remain explicit opt-in gates.
Keep fixtures deterministic with declared seeds/time seams, unique owned profile/storage/listener identities, exact current source identity and independent test order.
Treat flakiness as a defect. Retain the first failure and every retry; quarantine requires tracked owner/reason/expiry and cannot satisfy required closure.
Report skipped-not-applicable separately from blocked-environment, not-run, failed and passed. Missing applicable critical tests prevent completion.
Setup/teardown failure, native unconfirmed exit and artifact freshness mismatch invalidate the run; never hide them behind passing children.
realisticResourcePolicyProposal: One Playwright worker, no parallel AI/build/performance work.
Use small synthetic inputs and deterministic boundary workers for exhaustive UI branching; keep physical generation/training/model quality as separately named installed-model witnesses.

Retain approved memory guards and measured host budgets, including 3 GiB small CPU and 3.5 GiB larger CPU admission only for their exact pinned profiles; do not lower further as a testing convenience.
Separate cold startup and readiness, UI input-to-paint responsiveness, and long-running inference/training deadlines; a 30-minute model delivery budget is not an acceptable blocking UI response time.
Do not impose arbitrary global UI runtime targets. Freeze meaningful local baselines and prospective named-profile budgets before optimization, preserving original failures.
Use idempotent owned setup/teardown, interruption-safe immutable run directories and remaining-only reruns based on exact source and missing criterion identity.

No public marketplace, arbitrary workflows/imported code sandbox, hybrid synchronization or new advanced diagnostic UI
No new model/dependency/provider download or credential use without authority
